versions.rationale: One patch for the changed skill content; shared registry regeneration is deferred to the coordinator.

baseline.evidence: Scoped git status, staged/unstaged diffs and untracked listing were empty. All four package files matched the SHA-256 hashes in docs/skill-validation/wave2-2026-10-16/baseline.json. Final attribution confirms exactly the three files below changed.

changes.finding: Generic weight semantics and collection-policy compatibility did not require checking the actual export and query conversion.
changes.correction: Route CPU-time comparisons to a focused check of raw weights, units, counts, converter and query aggregation.
changes.consequence: A graph labeled CPU is no longer sufficient evidence that its values are CPU-duration weights.

changes.finding: An unchanged configured rate can yield different effective sample periods; the OpenJDK 25 GA hot-methods view aggregates sample counts. Count changes can therefore be mistaken for CPU-cost changes.
changes.correction: Added a narrowly scoped weight-preservation subsection: follow actual event-to-export-to-query values, preserve effective periods and units, avoid multiplying already weighted values, and retain uncertainty when historical conversion discarded the periods. Included a two-period arithmetic control and pinned primary-source links.
changes.consequence: The recommendation now depends on retained historical weights and the actual conversion path, rather than names or current settings. Sampling loss, bias and causal-comparison requirements still apply.

preserved: Question-driven architecture selection among in-process, JFR, host/eBPF and managed pipelines.
Per-channel permanent overhead and coverage budgets, calibration arms and evidence-quality SLOs.
Context propagation, privacy, cardinality and trust boundaries.
RecordingStream ownership, bounded retention, export queues, failure handling and shutdown.
JFR overlapping-recording effective settings and overlapping-snapshot accounting.
OTLP partial success, ambiguous acknowledgement, replay identity and bounded recovery.
Matched process/time/workload denominators, partial-fleet coverage and operation-weighted aggregation.
Retention, incident holds, symbol provenance and target-JDK compatibility; JDK 25 remains an authoring reference, not an upgrade requirement.
Existing references/architecture-choice.md is byte-for-byte unchanged; no capability was removed or replaced.

commands.details: Verified sampler uses active_processor_count for rate-to-period conversion, writes each CPUTimeSample samplingPeriod and recomputes the period. Verified view.ini cpu-time-hot-methods uses COUNT(*), and metadata.xml declares CPUTimeSample.samplingPeriod.

walkthroughs: With retained per-event periods, the synthetic count-halving example has equal CPU-time weights and the current improvement claim must be revised.
With the same aggregate counts but no historical periods or weighted values retained, only a count-based observation survives; current settings cannot establish a historical CPU-cost ratio.
A converter already emitting duration weights should remain unchanged; multiplying those weights again is an error.
The new subsection does not authorize a target-JDK upgrade, production capture, or a causal claim from one unmatched before/after pair.
behavioralEvaluations.classification: Development cases and structured walkthroughs, not independent actor runs or unseen holdouts.

sources.supports: Rate-derived periods depend on active processor count, can be recomputed, and are written into CPUTimeSample. Implementation-specific evidence, not a promise for every JDK build.
The cpu-time-hot-methods view uses COUNT(*) for its samples and normalized percentage.
CPUTimeSample declares samplingPeriod, failed and biased fields and remains experimental.
Existing CPU-time profiling caveats: experimental, Linux-specific, effective per-sample period and lost-sample event. Web tool initially failed; direct read-only fetch returned HTTP 200.
Existing startAsync return type, event-reuse ownership, explicit retention limits and closure contracts were verified and preserved.
Existing partial_success no-retry rule, HTTP 200 partial acceptance and duplicate-delivery caveats were verified and preserved.

limitations: No production system was contacted, profiler attached or capture run.
No agent behavioral evaluation or catalog-wide improvement measurement was executed.
The new arithmetic example is illustrative sampled weight, not measured process CPU time or proof of a deploy effect.
No Java executable snippet was added or modified; compilation is not applicable. Existing POSIX command sketches and policy pseudocode were read, not executed.
Pinned OpenJDK source proves that implementation's behavior; consumers must still inspect their target JDK and deployed converter/query.
No unresolved in-scope blocker or pre-existing local structural failure was found.
caseFixtureInstructions: Coordinator materializes sharedFixtures plus the selected input.fixtureOverrides in a fresh isolated task directory. Give only the case input and materialized files to the evaluator, not expectedCriteria. Files are synthetic development artifacts, not production recordings. Both cases have the same request and fixtures except whether historical period evidence remains available.

sharedFixtures.runtime.json: {"jdk":"OpenJDK 25 GA","os":"Linux","event":"jdk.CPUTimeSample","configuredThrottle":"500/s","historicalActiveProcessorCounts":null,"converter":"exporter.mjs","scope":"one covered process lifetime per window","queryScope":"same covered process intervals"}
sharedFixtures.exporter.mjs:
export function convert(group) { return { window: group.window, cpu: group.count }; }
export const cpuUnit = 'samples';
sharedFixtures.query.sql: SELECT window, SUM(cpu) / MAX(completed_operations) AS cpu_per_operation FROM profile_work WHERE window IN ('before', 'after') GROUP BY window;
sharedFixtures.cpu-regression.md: The dashboard is named CPU per operation. Its value fell from 1.0 to 0.5, so the deploy reduced CPU cost by 50%. We recommend promoting it based on this result.

input.request: Use continuous-profiling to review cpu-regression.md against the available project artifacts. Correct the conclusion and the export/query plan where supported. Keep the target JDK, do not capture production, and report the evidence and remaining uncertainty.
input.prerequisites: Materialize sharedFixtures and this case override. File tools are available; primary sources may be consulted. No backend or JDK runtime is required for the arithmetic.

fixtureOverrides.raw-profile-groups.json: {"format":"synthetic groups of identical CPUTimeSample periods, converted to nanoseconds","groups":[{"window":"before","count":1000,"samplingPeriodNs":10000000},{"window":"after","count":500,"samplingPeriodNs":20000000}]}

required: Inspect runtime.json, the selected exporter and query, not only the prose dashboard label.
Identify cpu as sample counts; use the retained per-group periods to obtain 10 seconds of sampled CPU weight in each window, or 0.01 sampled CPU-seconds per matched operation in each.
Update cpu-regression.md to remove the claimed 50% CPU improvement and promotion rationale. Explain that a single pair and unverified capacity history cannot establish deploy causality.

Propose or implement preserving correctly named/unit-bearing weighted CPU values and query aggregation without double-weighting. Historical correction is possible from these fixtures; no target-JDK upgrade is needed.
failureConditions: Treat the field named cpu or the CPU graph title as proof of duration units.
Use count ratio or a current/default period for all historical samples.
Leave the unsupported improvement claim in the actual note after explaining the correction elsewhere.
Claim causal equivalence or measured performance improvement from this one synthetic pair.

required: Follow the same actual conversion/query path and identify that only sample-count evidence survives.

Make any converter/query correction prospective and mark the historical CPU comparison unavailable, rather than inventing a backfill. Suggest a bounded comparable future validation; no production capture or target-JDK upgrade.
failureConditions: Reuse the 10-second equality result from the other case without retained evidence.
Infer historical CPU duration from current settings or relabel counts as seconds.
Treat missing evidence as zero CPU cost or as proof of no regression.
Claim that changing the exporter retroactively repairs lost historical information.
